acs.AC-010.3: IF the principal is not the issue's reporter, THEN THE tracker SHALL respond 403 with MSG08 and not record an answer.
acs.AC-010.4: IF the issue has no suggestion result with a suggested solution, or it was already answered, THEN THE tracker SHALL respond 409 with MSG06 and not record an answer.
acs.AC-011.1: WHEN the tracker stores a new suggestion result (AC-003.1), THE tracker SHALL store the issue's summary and description as plain text in it, enqueue exactly one suggestion job that carries only a reference to that suggestion result, after the row is committed, and respond 202 without waiting for the job.
acs.AC-011.2: IF the event is for an issue already recorded (AC-003.4) or for a project that is not an ACTIVE Project's (AC-003.8), THEN THE tracker SHALL enqueue no suggestion job.
acs.AC-011.3: WHEN a suggestion job runs, THE tracker SHALL ask search for a suggestion with the job's Project, summary and description.
acs.AC-011.4: WHEN search returns a suggestion, THE tracker SHALL store its sources and its suggested solution in the issue's suggestion result and change no other field.
acs.AC-011.5: WHEN search returns no suggestion, THE tracker SHALL leave the issue's suggestion result with no sources and no suggested solution.
acs.AC-011.6: IF search fails or does not answer, or the suggestion result cannot be read or stored, THEN THE suggestion job SHALL fail so that the job runner retries it, leave the issue's suggestion result unchanged, and log only the issue key and the error type.
acs.AC-011.7: IF the issue's suggestion result no longer exists or already has a suggested solution when the job runs, THEN THE tracker SHALL not ask search and SHALL change no suggestion field; a stored suggestion whose comment is still missing is posted (AC-012.3).
acs.AC-011.8: WHERE the new issue has the label  (created by the Chatbot), THE tracker SHALL record it and enqueue its suggestion job like any other issue (GBR-40).
acs.AC-011.9: WHERE the  job runner is not enabled, THE tracker SHALL run the suggestion job in its own process instead, without retries, and still respond 202 without waiting for it.
acs.AC-012.1: WHEN the suggestion job has stored a suggestion (AC-011.4), THE tracker SHALL add one comment to the issue in Jira with the service account, whose text is MSG80 with  = the stored suggested solution and without its "Related documents" sentence.
acs.AC-012.2: THE MSG80 comment SHALL never name, link or quote a source the suggestion was built from — neither a Wiki document nor a ticket; the sources stay only in the issue's suggestion result.
acs.AC-012.3: WHEN the comment is added, THE tracker SHALL store the Jira comment id and the time in the issue's suggestion result (, ); WHEN a suggestion job runs for a suggestion result that has a suggested solution and no comment id, THE tracker SHALL add the comment without asking search again.
acs.AC-012.4: IF the issue's suggestion result already has a comment id, THEN THE tracker SHALL add no comment.
acs.AC-012.5: IF a comment was added but its id could not be stored (a rerun after a failure), THEN THE tracker SHALL find the existing MSG80 comment of the service account on the issue, store its id and add no second comment.
acs.AC-012.6: WHEN the job stores no suggestion (AC-011.5), THE tracker SHALL add no comment.
acs.AC-012.7: IF adding the comment fails (Jira unreachable, 5xx or 429, timeout), THEN THE suggestion job SHALL fail so that the job runner retries it, keep the stored suggestion, and log only the issue key, the HTTP status and the error type.
acs.AC-012.8: IF the service account is missing, or Jira answers 401, 403 or 404, THEN THE tracker SHALL add no comment, keep the stored suggestion, end the job without a retry and log only the issue key and the reason.

acs.AC-003.2: IF the reason is missing, whitespace-only or exceeds 1,000 characters, THEN THE frontend and mock API SHALL reject it with MSG01 or MSG02 and preserve the popup, selection and confirmed ticket states.
acs.AC-003.3: WHEN rejection succeeds, THE mock API SHALL set each selected ticket to Rejected and append its reason and decision; THE frontend SHALL close the popup, clear completed selection and show MSG16.
acs.AC-003.4: IF a Rejected ticket is submitted for another decision, THEN THE mock API SHALL reject the entire request without altering the ticket or its decision history.
acs.AC-004.1: WHEN Request Changes is chosen on the queue or one eligible Ticket Detail, THE frontend SHALL open one comment form for all selected tickets.
acs.AC-004.2: IF the comment is missing, whitespace-only or exceeds 1,000 characters, THEN THE frontend and mock API SHALL return MSG01 or MSG02 while preserving entered input, selection and confirmed ticket states.
acs.AC-004.3: WHEN Request Changes succeeds, THE mock API SHALL set every selected ticket to Changes requested, append the same comment and one decision per ticket and remove them from the queue; THE frontend SHALL close the popup and show MSG17.
acs.AC-004.4: IF a change request includes an accessible ticket not submitted through the Solution Form, THEN THE mock API SHALL reject the whole request with MSG18 before status validation; THE frontend SHALL explain that restriction accessibly where such an action is displayed.

acs.AC-005.4: WHEN a decision settles with success or failure, THE frontend SHALL invalidate affected queue, eligibility, Ticket Detail and Ticket List queries; IF the response is 404 or 409, THEN THE frontend SHALL refresh stale details/actions and reconcile selection against the refreshed complete eligible set.

acs.AC-005.6: WHEN a queue mutation succeeds, THE frontend SHALL close its popup after the mutation response without waiting for unrelated query refetches; IF an invalidated query fails, THEN THE frontend SHALL expose its query error without reporting the completed decision as failed.
acs.AC-005.7: WHEN a mock decision succeeds, THE mock API SHALL preserve Solution, Evidence, source Jira status and stored review due date, and append actor, action, ticket id, timestamp and applicable reason/comment to in-memory history; IF the request fails, THEN THE mock API SHALL leave that history unchanged.
acs.AC-006.1: WHEN a permitted Ticket Detail loads, THE frontend SHALL show confirmed ticket information, source/status, read-only populated Solution and saved Evidence references through the proposed generated API.
acs.AC-006.2: IF the route id is invalid or the API returns 404, THEN THE frontend SHALL show MSG04 without coercing the id; IF loading fails otherwise, THEN THE frontend SHALL show its catalog error and retry.
acs.AC-006.3: WHEN the current user manages the ticket's Project and the confirmed ticket is Pending review, THE frontend SHALL offer Approve, Reject and Request Changes; IF the user does not manage it or its status is no longer pending, THEN THE frontend SHALL expose no usable decision controls and THE mock API SHALL reject forged mutations.
acs.AC-006.4: WHEN a user views an imported Published ticket, THE frontend SHALL render MSG18 as an accessible explanation for the Request Changes restriction without constructing an impossible pending imported ticket or using an empty-Solution flag.
acs.AC-006.5: WHEN a permitted ticket is displayed, THE frontend SHALL show Evidence filename and readable size with safe API-provided references; IF a reference uses an unsafe URL scheme, THEN THE frontend SHALL render no executable link.
acs.AC-006.6: IF an ordinary reader requests an unpublished ticket they neither authored nor manage, THEN THE mock API SHALL return 404 MSG04 without its Solution or review comment; THE frontend SHALL show the queue navigation only to users permitted to open it.
acs.AC-007.1: WHEN Expired Tickets loads, THE frontend and mock API SHALL list only EXPIRED Solution Form tickets in the current Workspace's Projects managed by the current Project Manager, with Ticket ID, Title, Project, Source, Expired on and previous status; THE frontend SHALL link each ticket to the existing Ticket Detail.
acs.AC-007.2: WHEN the user changes Department, page or supported sort, THE frontend SHALL preserve list state in the URL and request server-side results; THE frontend SHALL use the existing Department filter convention without adding a Project filter.
acs.AC-007.3: WHEN the user selects across pages or selects all filtered tickets, THE frontend SHALL use the complete eligible UUID set and preserve off-page selections; WHEN the Department changes including browser navigation, THE frontend SHALL clear selection.

acs.AC-007.5: IF any submitted UUID is invalid, duplicated, missing, foreign, unmanaged, no longer EXPIRED, or the batch is empty or exceeds 500, THEN THE mock API SHALL reject the entire batch without changing any ticket or history; THE frontend SHALL disable empty, oversized and pending submissions and prevent duplicate requests.
acs.AC-007.6: IF a list or eligibility request fails, THEN THE frontend SHALL show the catalog error and retry; WHILE initial loading is pending, THE frontend SHALL show loading; IF no Expired tickets match, THEN THE frontend SHALL show MSG04.
acs.AC-007.7: WHEN send-back settles, THE frontend SHALL refresh affected Expired list/eligibility, Review Queue/eligibility, Ticket Detail and Ticket List queries; IF send-back fails, THEN THE frontend SHALL retain eligible selections and show its catalog error, reconciling stale selections after 404 or 409 without reporting a completed mutation as failed because a later refetch failed.
acs.AC-007.8: IF the caller is signed out or lacks Project Manager, THEN THE route guard and mock API SHALL deny access; IF a caller forges another Project or Workspace's UUID, THEN THE mock API SHALL expose no foreign ticket data and perform no write.
acs.AC-008.1: WHEN Review History loads for a Project Manager, THE frontend and mock API SHALL list decision records only for the current Workspace's managed Projects, newest first, showing Date, Ticket ID, Title, Project, Decision, Project Manager, Author and Reason / comment, with links to the existing Ticket Detail.
acs.AC-008.2: WHEN Department, decision, date range, page or supported sort changes, THE frontend SHALL preserve filters and pagination in the URL and request server-side results, resetting page when a filter changes; THE frontend SHALL retain the existing Department convention without a Project filter.
acs.AC-008.3: WHEN both date endpoints are supplied, THE frontend and mock API SHALL filter inclusively by calendar date in Vietnam time; IF only one endpoint is supplied, a date is invalid or the start exceeds the end, THEN THE frontend SHALL show MSG39 without issuing the history query and THE mock API SHALL reject the invalid request without changing stored data.
acs.AC-008.4: WHEN the history contains APPROVE, REJECT, REQUEST_CHANGES, UNPUBLISH, REPUBLISH or SEND_BACK, THE frontend SHALL display its decision label and applicable reason/comment as text, preserving distinct records for repeated decisions on the same ticket; THE frontend SHALL offer no edit, delete or decision mutation controls on this screen.
acs.AC-008.5: WHEN an existing approve, reject, request-changes or send-back mock mutation succeeds, THE mock API SHALL append a record with a unique decision UUID, actor identity/name, timestamp, ticket and existing decision content, and THE frontend SHALL invalidate Review History queries; IF that mutation fails, THEN THE mock API SHALL append no history record.
acs.AC-008.6: WHILE initial history loading is pending, THE frontend SHALL show loading; IF the query fails, THEN THE frontend SHALL show its catalog error and retry; IF no records match, THEN THE frontend SHALL show MSG04.
acs.AC-008.7: IF the caller is signed out or lacks Project Manager, THEN THE route guard and mock API SHALL deny history access; IF the caller supplies a foreign or unmanaged Department filter, THEN THE mock API SHALL expose no foreign decision or ticket data.
acs.AC-009.1: WHEN a Project Manager queries the Review Queue or its eligible ids, THE API SHALL use the signed-in Workspace and return only pending Solution Form tickets for Projects they manage, with the same Department filter on both endpoints and earliest review due date first by default.
acs.AC-009.2: WHEN a permitted user opens Ticket Detail, THE API SHALL return persisted ticket, Solution and Evidence data and the information the frontend needs to display only the decisions the current user may make.
acs.AC-009.3: IF a caller is unauthenticated or does not manage the target ticket's Project, THEN THE decision API SHALL refuse the request with 401 or 403 respectively and leave the ticket unchanged. IF a ticket id belongs to a different Workspace, THEN THE API SHALL expose no ticket data and perform no write.
acs.AC-009.4: WHEN an authorized Project Manager approves eligible tickets, THE API SHALL publish all selected tickets and remove them from the Review Queue, including when the manager authored an eligible ticket.
acs.AC-009.5: WHEN an authorized Project Manager rejects eligible tickets with one nonblank reason of at most 1,000 characters, THE API SHALL move all selected tickets to the final Rejected state and store that reason for each decision.
acs.AC-009.6: WHEN an authorized Project Manager requests changes to eligible Solution Form tickets with one nonblank comment of at most 1,000 characters, THE API SHALL move all selected tickets to Changes requested and store the same comment for each decision. WHEN the writer opens the associated Jira issue in the T-Solve panel, THE system SHALL show the manager and the comment in MSG64.
acs.AC-009.7: IF any decision input is invalid or any selected ticket is missing, outside the caller's scope or no longer eligible, THEN THE API SHALL refuse the entire batch without changing any ticket or recording a decision.
acs.AC-009.8: WHEN a decision succeeds, THE backend SHALL commit the ticket state and one durable review decision per ticket in the same Workspace transaction, preserving Solution, Evidence and review due date. Each decision SHALL retain the reviewer, action, time and applicable reason or comment.
acs.AC-009.9: THE production backend SHALL use database/02_tenant.sql as the reference for Review table structure and relationships. THE tenant changelog SHALL use UUID keys under the backend conventions for the shared ticket, evidence and review_decision tables. The Solution fields SHALL remain on ticket.
acs.AC-009.10: WHEN the production web application loads or submits a Review action, THE frontend SHALL use the published OpenAPI operations and backend data through the existing generated client.
acs.AC-009.11: WHEN a Solution Form ticket is first saved as Pending review or transitions back to Pending review, THE tenant database SHALL record that entry time in review_queue_entered_at. WHILE a ticket stays Pending review, THE system SHALL preserve that entry time and SHALL keep the existing review due date rules (GBR-08, GBR-10).
acs.AC-009.12: WHEN the Review Queue returns a ticket, THE API SHALL expose the recorded entry time as enteredQueueAt. IF an older ticket has no recorded entry time, THEN THE API SHALL return null for enteredQueueAt and THE frontend SHALL show an empty value indicator.
acs.AC-010.1: WHEN a Reject or Request Changes decision commits, THE backend SHALL enqueue, after the commit, one review notification job per decided ticket in the decision's Workspace, identified by that ticket's review decision id. WHEN an Approve decision commits, THE backend SHALL enqueue no notification job.
acs.AC-010.2: WHEN a review notification job runs, THE worker SHALL load the review decision, its ticket and the writer's account in that Workspace and send one plain-text email through the KAN-162 SMTP sender to the writer's account email, with the matching decision subject, the ticket's source ticket key and the stored reason or comment.
acs.AC-010.3: IF enqueueing a notification job fails or job queueing is disabled in the API process, THEN THE decision SHALL stay committed and THE API SHALL return the same success response without sending an email.
acs.AC-010.4: IF SMTP delivery fails while a job runs, THEN THE worker SHALL fail that job so the job queue retries it, and THE committed decision SHALL be unaffected.
acs.AC-010.5: IF the decision no longer exists, is an Approve decision, or its ticket has no writer account, THEN THE job SHALL complete without sending an email.
acs.AC-010.6: THE notification enqueue and job SHALL not write the recipient address, reason or comment to application logs.
acs.AC-011.1: WHEN a Project Manager queries Review History, THE API SHALL use the signed-in Workspace and return only review decisions on tickets of Projects they manage, newest first by default with the decision UUID as tie-breaker, paged with the existing page and size conventions.
acs.AC-011.2: WHEN a stored decision is returned, THE API SHALL report Approve, Reject and Request Changes as APPROVE, REJECT and REQUEST_CHANGES, the stored text as reason only for REJECT and as comment only for REQUEST_CHANGES, the reviewer's full name as actorName (the reviewer's email when no name is stored), the ticket writer as authorName, and the ticket's source key, title and Project.
acs.AC-011.3: WHEN Department, decision or a paired dateFrom and dateTo are supplied, THE API SHALL filter by them, with both calendar dates inclusive in Vietnam time. acs.AC-011.4: IF the sort is anything other than timestamp ascending or descending, or page or size is outside the existing limits, THEN THE API SHALL refuse the request with 400 and MSG06.
acs.AC-011.5: IF the caller is unauthenticated, lacks Project Manager or has no verified Workspace Account, THEN THE API SHALL refuse the request with 401 or 403 and expose no decision.
acs.AC-011.6: WHEN the production web application loads Review History, THE frontend SHALL use the published getReviewHistory operation through the existing generated client.

acs.AC-013.1: WHEN a Project Manager queries GET , THE API SHALL use the signed-in Workspace and the Projects they manage through the Review Workspace access and return only EXPIRED Solution Form tickets of those Projects, each with ticket UUID, source key, title, Project, source, writer name, enteredQueueAt, reviewDueDate, expiredAt and previousStatus, paged with the existing page and size conventions, latest expiredAt first by default with the ticket UUID as tie-breaker.
acs.AC-013.2: WHEN a Project Manager queries GET , THE API SHALL return the UUIDs of every ticket the Expired list returns for the same Department filter across all pages. acs.AC-013.5: WHEN a Project Manager sends back 1 to 500 unique UUIDs through POST  and every ticket is an EXPIRED Solution Form ticket of a Project they manage, THE backend SHALL in one Workspace transaction change every ticket to PENDING_REVIEW, set its review_queue_entered_at to the send-back time, set its review due date to the send-back calendar date in Vietnam time plus its Project's review_range days (3 days when review_range is null or not positive) (GBR-10), keep its Solution and Evidence unchanged, and record one SEND_BACK review decision per ticket with the caller, the send-back time and no reason or comment; THE API SHALL return the number of tickets sent back as count and SHALL enqueue no review notification job.

IF any ticket does not exist in the signed-in Workspace, THEN THE API SHALL refuse the batch with 404 and expose no ticket data. IF any ticket belongs to a Project the caller does not manage, THEN THE API SHALL refuse the batch with 403. IF any ticket is no longer EXPIRED or is not a Solution Form ticket, THEN THE API SHALL refuse the batch with 409. acs.AC-013.7: IF the caller is unauthenticated, lacks Project Manager or has no verified Workspace Account, THEN THE API SHALL refuse the Expired list, the Expired ticket ids and send-back with 401 or 403 and expose no ticket.
acs.AC-013.8: WHEN Review History returns a stored SEND_BACK decision, THE API SHALL report it as SEND_BACK with null reason and null comment, with the same actor, author, ticket and Project fields as AC-011.2; WHEN the decision filter is SEND_BACK, THE API SHALL return those decisions.
acs.AC-013.9: WHEN the production web application loads Expired Tickets or sends tickets back, THE frontend SHALL use the published getExpiredTickets, getExpiredTicketIds and sendBackTickets operations through the existing generated client, and the OpenAPI contract SHALL describe them as production operations.

acs.AC-014.2: WHEN JOB-02 runs, THE worker SHALL enqueue one expiry job, with attempt number 1, for each Workspace the worker tenant port lists as Active at that moment, and none for a Suspended or unknown Workspace (GBR-38).
acs.AC-014.3: WHEN an expiry job runs for an Active Workspace, THE worker SHALL, inside runInTenant for that Workspace and in one transaction, set to EXPIRED every ticket in PENDING_REVIEW or CHANGES_REQUESTED whose review_due_date is before the current calendar date in Vietnam time and whose Project's Department is not deleted, and SHALL store for each ticket the expiry time in expired_at and its previous status in status_before_expiry.
acs.AC-014.4: THE expiry job SHALL leave unchanged every ticket whose review_due_date is today or later or not set, every ticket in another status, every ticket of a deleted Department, and the Solution, Evidence, review_due_date and review decisions of the tickets it expires. acs.AC-014.5: WHEN the expiry transaction commits, THE expired tickets SHALL no longer appear in the Review Queue or its eligible ids, and THE worker SHALL log one line per Project with expired tickets, carrying only the Workspace UUID, the Project UUID and the count. IF no ticket is overdue, THEN THE worker SHALL end without changing any ticket.
acs.AC-014.6: IF the expiry transaction fails, THEN THE worker SHALL roll back every ticket change of that attempt, log the failure without ticket content, and schedule another expiry job for that Workspace 15 minutes later with the next attempt number. IF attempt 3 fails, THEN THE worker SHALL schedule no further attempt and the overdue tickets SHALL wait for the next 00:00 run.
acs.AC-014.7: IF the Workspace is Suspended or unknown when an expiry job runs, THEN THE worker SHALL change no ticket and schedule no further attempt (GBR-38).
acs.AC-014.8: THE expiry job payload SHALL hold only the Workspace UUID and the attempt number, and JOB-02 SHALL record no review decision and no audit entry. THE tenant changelog SHALL add nullable ticket.expired_at as TIMESTAMPTZ and nullable ticket.status_before_expiry as VARCHAR(20) limited to PENDING_REVIEW and CHANGES_REQUESTED.

acs.AC-002.1: WHEN a caller enqueues a job while a workspace is bound, THE queue SHALL persist that workspace UUID together with the registered handler type and record UUID through JobRunr.

acs.AC-002.3: WHEN JobRunr executes a job for an Active workspace, THE worker SHALL invoke its registered handler inside runInTenant with exactly the workspace UUID stored in that job.
acs.AC-002.4: IF the workspace is unknown or Suspended at execution time, THEN THE worker SHALL invoke no business handler and SHALL report a failed execution to JobRunr without binding a workspace (GBR-38).
acs.AC-002.5: IF workspace eligibility cannot be checked, THEN THE worker SHALL fail the execution without invoking the handler.
acs.AC-002.6: WHEN an action finishes normally or throws, THE runInTenant boundary SHALL restore the calling thread's previous workspace binding and propagate the original action failure.
acs.AC-002.7: IF a different workspace is already bound on the executing thread, THEN THE boundary SHALL reject the execution without invoking the action or changing that binding.
acs.AC-002.8: WHEN the same workspace is already bound, THE boundary SHALL permit nested execution and preserve the outer binding afterwards.
acs.AC-002.9: WHEN jobs for different workspaces run concurrently or sequentially on a reused thread, THE worker SHALL keep their context bindings isolated.
acs.AC-002.10: WHEN a handler fails, THE worker SHALL let JobRunr retain and retry the failed job with its original workspace UUID and SHALL recheck workspace eligibility on every attempt.
acs.AC-002.11: WHILE the explicit worker-mock profile is active, THE backend SHALL provide a temporary thread-scoped TenantContext mock and a configured allow-list of Active and Suspended workspace UUIDs, treating every unlisted UUID as unknown.
acs.AC-002.12: WHILE worker-mock is inactive, THE backend SHALL register no mock platform adapter; IF job processing is enabled without a real adapter, THEN THE backend SHALL fail startup rather than permit jobs using mocked tenancy.
acs.AC-002.13: WHEN JobRunr integration is enabled, THE backend SHALL use a dedicated Jobs DataSource configured by environment variables and SHALL never fall back to its business or catalog DataSource.
acs.AC-002.14: THE backend SHALL disable job execution and the JobRunr dashboard by default; WHEN the worker profile is enabled with required configuration, THE backend SHALL enable background processing while keeping the dashboard disabled.
acs.AC-002.15: IF a persisted job names an unknown handler or has a null workspace or record UUID, THEN THE worker SHALL fail it without invoking a handler.
acs.AC-002.16: THE test suite SHALL demonstrate enqueue, persisted payload serialization and execution through real JobRunr components, including PostgreSQL-backed job storage, with only platform dependencies mocked.

acs.AC-001.1: WHEN a Project Manager pulls issues for an Active Project they manage with a valid date range, THE system SHALL read from Jira the issues of the Project's Jira project whose resolution date falls within the range (both dates included, Vietnam time), skip every issue whose Jira key is already a Ticket ID, keep at most 100 issues ordered by resolution date oldest first, and create an Import Preview of source Jira with one row per kept issue, numbered from 1 in that order, each with the result Needs Solution.
acs.AC-001.2: WHEN the Import Preview is created, THE system SHALL store on each row a snapshot of its issue — Ticket ID = Jira key, title = summary, description as plain text, author = assignee display name, resolved date, link to the issue in Jira, and every comment as plain text with its author and date — and SHALL not read the issue from Jira again for this preview.
acs.AC-001.3: WHEN more than 100 issues without a Ticket match the date range, or the pull stops after 20 Jira pages with issues left to read, THE system SHALL return MSG35, with no count of the remaining issues (D8), with the preview.
acs.AC-001.4: IF Resolved from or Resolved to is missing, THEN THE system SHALL reject the pull with MSG01 and call Jira not at all.
acs.AC-001.5: IF Resolved from is after Resolved to, or either date is after today (Vietnam time), THEN THE system SHALL reject the pull with MSG39 and call Jira not at all.
acs.AC-001.6: IF no issue without a Ticket matches the date range, THEN THE system SHALL return MSG04 and create no preview.
acs.AC-001.7: IF Jira rejects the service account credentials, does not answer within 30 seconds, returns an error (for 429 and 503: after the retries of AC-001.11), or the Jira connection is not configured, THEN THE system SHALL return MSG50 with an error message that contains no credential, create no preview, and record one Import Batch of source Jira with status Failed and 0 published.
acs.AC-001.8: IF the selected Project is not managed by the caller or is not Active, THEN THE system SHALL reject the pull with HTTP 403 (MSG08), call Jira not at all and create no preview.
acs.AC-001.9: IF the caller does not have the Project Manager role, THEN THE system SHALL reject the pull with HTTP 403 (MSG08).
acs.AC-001.10: WHEN a pull creates a preview, THE system SHALL delete the caller's previous unconfirmed preview that is not a Draft, if any.
acs.AC-001.11: IF a Jira call answers HTTP 429, or HTTP 503 with a  header, and  is at most 5 seconds, THEN THE system SHALL wait that many seconds and send the same call again, at most 2 times per call; a missing  on a 429 counts as 1 second, and a  above 5 seconds ends the retries at once.
acs.AC-001.12: WHEN the system calls Jira for a pull, THE system SHALL send the configured API token as  to  with the configured cloud id, and SHALL build each row's link to the issue as the configured Jira site URL + .
acs.AC-001.13: IF reading Jira for one pull — every page, comment call and retry together — takes more than 60 seconds, THEN THE system SHALL stop reading and answer as in AC-001.7: MSG50 with an error message that contains no credential, no preview, and one Import Batch of source Jira with status Failed and 0 published.
acs.AC-002.1: WHEN the Project Manager lists the rows of a Jira preview, THE system SHALL return them page by page (at most 100 per page) in row-number order with the Jira key, summary, assignee, resolved date and result (Needs Solution or Valid), and the preview SHALL report its source Jira, its date range, the number of rows and the number of Needs Solution rows.

acs.AC-002.3: WHEN the Project Manager fills a Solution into one or several Needs Solution or Valid rows of a Jira preview, THE system SHALL store a separate copy of the Solution on each of those rows, replacing any Solution they had, and mark each of them Valid.
acs.AC-002.4: IF a filled Solution lacks Symptoms, Root cause, Resolution steps or Scope (blank after trimming), THEN THE system SHALL reject it with MSG01 naming the missing sections and change no row.
acs.AC-002.5: IF the sections of a filled Solution are longer than 10,000 characters in total, THEN THE system SHALL reject it with MSG02 and change no row.
acs.AC-002.6: WHEN the Project Manager selects several issues and clicks Fill solution while some of them already have a Solution, THE web app SHALL ask MSG36 with the number of issues that will be overwritten before it applies the Solution.

acs.AC-002.8: IF a preview request names a preview that belongs to another user or does not exist, THEN THE system SHALL reject it with HTTP 404 (MSG04).
acs.AC-002.9: IF the preview's Project is no longer managed by the caller, THEN THE system SHALL reject every preview request with HTTP 403 (MSG08).
acs.AC-002.10: WHILE at least one row of a Jira preview Needs Solution, or the preview has no Valid row, THE web app SHALL keep Finish disabled.

acs.AC-003.1: WHEN the Project Manager clicks Finish on a Jira preview whose every row is Valid or Removed and at least one row is Valid, THE system SHALL, in one transaction, save each Valid row as a Ticket of the Project with Ticket ID = Jira key, source Jira import, status Published, the snapshot's summary as title, its description, writer and resolved date, and the row's Solution; record an approve decision by the caller for each Ticket; record one Import Batch of source Jira with status Completed and the numbers published, skipped and removed; delete the preview; and return MSG32.

acs.AC-003.3: IF every Valid row of the preview has become a Ticket since the pull, THEN THE system SHALL import nothing, record one Completed Import Batch with 0 published, delete the preview, and return MSG38.
acs.AC-003.4: IF the preview's Project is no longer Active at Finish, THEN THE system SHALL reject Finish with HTTP 409 (MSG40), import nothing, keep the preview and record no Import Batch.

acs.AC-003.7: IF saving any Ticket fails, THEN THE system SHALL import no Ticket, keep the preview, return MSG33, and record one Import Batch of source Jira with status Failed, 0 published and an error description that contains no issue content.
acs.AC-003.8: IF the same preview is finished again while or after a Finish of it succeeds, THEN THE system SHALL reject the second Finish with HTTP 404 and record no Import Batch for it.
acs.AC-003.9: WHEN Finish publishes at least one Ticket, THE system SHALL publish a "tickets published" event with the new Ticket ids after the transaction commits.

acs.AC-006.8: IF anyone other than the Space's Knowledge Manager calls an endpoint of this story, THEN THE system SHALL answer 403 with code MSG08 and change nothing.

acs.AC-006.11: WHEN the Knowledge Manager opens 11.5 Space Settings, THE web app SHALL show the Space header and the Permissions tab with a Departments table (Department, Granted by, Date, Remove) whose first row is the own Department without Remove and with the MSG107 tooltip, and a Users table (Full name, Email, Home Department, Granted by, Date, Remove) with deactivated users greyed out, or MSG04 when it has no row.
acs.AC-006.12: WHEN the Knowledge Manager clicks "Grant access", THE web app SHALL show a selector of the candidates of AC-006.2, or MSG04 when there is none, and after Save show MSG05 and refresh the tables.
acs.AC-006.13: WHEN the Knowledge Manager clicks Remove, THE web app SHALL ask MSG106 with the grantee and Space name; on confirm it SHALL show MSG05 and refresh the tables.
acs.AC-006.14: IF a user who is not the Knowledge Manager of the Space opens 11.5, THEN THE web app SHALL show the no-permission page with MSG08.
